statement: Consider one consecutive transition in an admissible family, with scale ratio ℓ = m+/m− = mα+o(1), where α > 0 is fixed. Fix finite retained parent and child coordinate sets and an adjacency power η > 0. Let d be any complex array on the parent sets, and let MI+ project onto the retained set in child bin I+. The output in that bin is cI+ = MI+ Pm+,I+ Sm−,I− dI− , I+ ⊂ I−. 76 Suppose each active child index has at most k ≥ 1 active parents in its parent time bin satisfying |νb − νv| ≤ mη θ+, |zb − zv − (tIb − tIv )Uνv | ≤ mη w−. Thus k counts nearby pairs of retained coordinates, independently of whether their coefficients vanish. The displayed operator still uses every matrix entry between the retained sets. Then r+w2 + X b |cb|4 ≤ mo(1) k r−w2 − X v |dv|4 . (6.14) For each fixed complexity range, α, and η, and every ε > 0, the factor mo(1) may be replaced by Cεmε for all sufficiently large m in the window mα/2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m3α/2 . The constant and the lower threshold within this window are uniform. A family’s entry into the window may depend on the rate at which logm ℓ tends to α.
